Command: Do not put frankincense on a sotah meal offering
Summary: The command: Do not put frankincense on a sotah meal offering (Numbers 5:15). The jealousy offering of barley meal carried no oil and no frankincense, for it was an offering of memorial bringing iniquity to remembrance.
Commandment: Do not put frankincense on a sotah meal offering.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. This procedure belongs entirely to Israel's theocratic court: it was a public ordeal for a case no witness could settle, and it has no Christian counterpart — the New Testament settles suspected adultery by witness, confession, and church discipline (Matthew 18:15-17; John 8:3-11, where Jesus refuses a trap trial).
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: the procedure gave a suspected wife a public, God-decided vindication instead of a husband's private vengeance. Scripture states the procedure without a stated reason beyond the spirit of jealousy coming upon the husband (Numbers 5:14,30).
Function: The jealousy offering of barley meal carried no oil and no frankincense — a ceremonial law of the stripped offering. Its goal was to keep the sotah's meal plain in every way, no sweet fragrance on an offering that remembered sin. Scripture gives no particular evil this restrained beyond the rite itself, and I will not invent one; its work was order and meaning, not restraint. The barley without frankincense said the case was grave, and the offering matched it.
